issues.claim: A linked source from `CreateLinkedTokenSource` registers a callback on every parent token; until it is released with `Dispose`, a long-lived parent keeps those registrations and the linked source itself in memory
issues.problem: This matches how the runtime works, and I believe it is correct. The fetched CreateLinkedTokenSource excerpt cuts off before any remarks and says nothing about registrations, Dispose or the memory consequence. The generator also admits the Learn page may not state it. The explanation presents the 'memory leak that grows with the number of requests' as fact, but none of the three cited links shows it. Per the checks, the claim is unsupported by the provided evidence.
issues.suggestedFix: Add a source that states it, for example the CancellationTokenSource class page (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.threading.cancellationtokensource, remarks on Dispose) or the 'Cancellation in managed threads' article. Otherwise word the explanation as implementation behaviour ('the parent's registration list references the linked source, so it is not collected until Dispose or until the parent itself is unreachable') and stop attributing it to the three cited pages. Re-verify against the full page text.

issues.claim: you should reset only a source whose token nobody else uses any more
issues.problem: The TryReset remarks say it is for the sole owner when the operation has completed, no one else will attempt to cancel it, and any remaining registrations are erroneous. The same remarks explicitly allow other components to still hold the token and poll it after the reset. 'Nobody else uses the token any more' is stricter than the docs, and the ru text has the same wording.
issues.suggestedFix: Rephrase in both locales as 'only the sole owner should reset a source, once the operation has finished and nobody else will cancel it or rely on registrations on its token'.

issues.claim: Can a token that someone has already seen as cancelled become uncancelled again?
issues.problem: For a multi question the hint nearly gives away that option d is false, and it also points at the direction of cancellation for option b. It is strong, but it does not reveal the full correct set.
issues.suggestedFix: Weaken it, for example: 'Think about what the linked source is subscribed to, what has to happen to registrations when a source is no longer needed, and whether the cancelled state is reversible.'
